chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (AS), who said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when He willed to create Adam (AS), sent Jibra'il (AS) in the first hour of Friday. He grabbed with his right hand a handful that extended from the seventh heaven down to the lowest heaven, and took some soil from each heaven. He grabbed another handful from the seventh earth, the highest, to the seventh earth, the farthest.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Word, and it held the first handful in the right hand and the second handful in the left hand, and split the clay into two portions, scattering from the earth and from the heavens. He said to those in his right hand: From you come the Messengers, Prophets, successors, truthful ones, believers, the blessed, and those whose honor I will — so it became binding for them what He said, as He said.

And He said to those in his left hand: From you come the tyrants, polytheists, disbelievers, despots, and those whose humiliation and misery I will — so it became binding for them what He said, as He said. Then the two clays were mixed together.

This is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Verily, Allah is the Splitter of the seed and the stone' — the seed (hab) is the clay of the believers upon which Allah cast His love, and the stone (nawa) is the clay of the disbelievers who were distant from every good; and it was called nawa because it was far (na'a) from every good and remote from it.

And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'He brings forth the living from the dead and the Extractor of the dead from the living' — so the living is the believer whose clay emerges from the clay of the disbeliever, and the dead who emerges from the living is the disbeliever who emerges from the clay of the believer; thus the living is the believer and the dead is the disbeliever. And this is His word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Is he who was dead and We gave him life?' — his death was the mixing of his clay with the clay of the disbeliever, and his life was when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, separated them by His Word.

Likewise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings out the believer at birth from darkness after his entry into it, toward the light; and He brings out the disbeliever from light toward darkness after his entry into the light. This is His word, the Mighty and Majestic: 'That it may warn whoever is alive, and that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.'

key_terms.طِينَةُ الْكَافِرِينَ: Tinat al-kafirin — the clay of the disbelievers; primordial substance characterized by distance from all goodness
key_terms.طِينَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Tinat al-mu'minin — the clay of the believers; primordial substance from which believers were fashioned, upon which Allah cast His love
key_terms.فَالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى: Faliq al-habb wa al-nawa — Splitter of the seed and the stone (Quran 6:95); interpreted as splitting primordial clay into believer and disbeliever portions
key_terms.كَلِمَتَهُ: Kalimatuhu — His Word; the divine command that held and separated the primordial clay portions
key_terms.يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ: Yukhriyu al-hayya mina al-mayyit — bringing forth the living from the dead (Quran 6:95); the believer (living) emerging from disbeliever clay

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Kafi about the creation of Adam and primordial clay (tinat) of believers and disbelievers teach?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that when Allah willed to create Adam, He sent Jibra'il on Friday to gather clay spanning all seven heavens and all seven earths. Allah then commanded His Word to hold the first handful in the right hand — from which come the Messengers, Prophets, successors, truthful ones, believers, and the blessed — and the second handful in the left — from which come the tyrants, polytheists, disbelievers, and despots. The two clays were then mixed together, explaining why believers can emerge from disbeliever lineages and vice versa. Three Quranic verses are cited as evidence: the splitting of seed and stone (6:95), bringing the living from the dead (6:95), and the warning to the living (36:70).
